questions.stem: This tracing aligns arterial blood pressure with respiration and shows an exaggerated inspiratory fall in systolic pressure. In a patient with this finding, what is the most likely underlying condition?

explanation.summary: The tracing shows pulsus paradoxus, an inspiratory drop in systolic pressure exceeding 10 mmHg. It classically indicates cardiac tamponade (and also severe asthma or constrictive physiology), where inspiratory augmentation of RV filling compresses the LV and reduces stroke volume.
explanation.whyCorrect: The tracing shows pulsus paradoxus, an inspiratory drop in systolic pressure exceeding 10 mmHg. questions.stem: On this chest radiograph, the arrows outline a thin curvilinear density surrounding the cardiac silhouette. In the setting of constrictive pericarditis, what does this finding represent?

explanation.summary: A rim of calcification tracing the cardiac border is a classic radiographic clue to chronic constrictive pericarditis, reflecting long-standing pericardial inflammation and fibrocalcific thickening.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rim of calcification tracing the cardiac border is a classic radiographic clue to chronic constrictive pericarditis, reflecting long-standing pericardial inflammation and fibrocalcific thickening.

questions.stem: The insets contrast a normal pericardium with the result after the outlined structure is surgically removed. In constrictive pericarditis, why is removing this layer therapeutic?

choices.label: A
choices.text: It drains an infected pleural effusion compressing the lung

choices.label: B
choices.text: It eliminates the rigid, thickened sac that restricts diastolic filling

choices.label: C
choices.text: It relieves coronary artery obstruction limiting myocardial perfusion

choices.label: D
choices.text: It repairs an incompetent valve causing regurgitation

choices.label: E
choices.text: It resects hypertrophied myocardium obstructing outflow

explanation.summary: In constrictive pericarditis the fibrotic, rigid pericardium encases the heart and prevents adequate diastolic filling; pericardiectomy (removal of the pericardium) frees the ventricles to fill normally, relieving the constriction.
explanation.whyCorrect: In constrictive pericarditis the fibrotic, rigid pericardium encases the heart and prevents adequate diastolic filling; pericardiectomy (removal of the pericardium) frees the ventricles to fill normally, relieving the constriction.

questions.stem: This tracing shows left and right ventricular volumes across the respiratory cycle in constrictive pericarditis, with the two ventricles filling reciprocally. What phenomenon does this illustrate?

choices.label: C
choices.text: Left bundle branch block delaying LV contraction

explanation.summary: A rigid pericardium fixes total cardiac volume, so inspiratory increases in right ventricular filling occur at the expense of left ventricular filling (and the reverse on expiration); this exaggerated ventricular interdependence underlies the discordant volume changes and the respiratory variation seen in constriction.
explanation.whyCorrect: A rigid pericardium fixes total cardiac volume, so inspiratory increases in right ventricular filling occur at the expense of left ventricular filling (and the reverse on expiration); this exaggerated ventricular interdependence underlies the discordant volume changes and the respiratory variation seen in constriction.
